As Plastikman he made long, sparse tracks built around the TB-303.
He launched the Minus label in 1998 and was an early adopter of laptop DJing.

influencedBy.why: His Plastikman records are built around the TB-303 sound they discovered.
Hawtin's stripped-down techno follows the minimal path Mills set out.
Detroit techno across the river was his formative influence.
Atkins's Detroit techno set his starting point.
Kraftwerk's minimal machine music underlies his approach.

cousins.why: Music built on stripping things down and holding a single idea.
Repetition used to build tension over long tracks.

artists.name: 808 State
artists.summary: A Manchester group that turned Chicago acid house into British chart music. Pacific State became one of the defining records of the UK rave era.
know: They formed around the Eastern Bloc record shop with Graham Massey, Martin Price and Gerald Simpson.
Pacific State reached the UK top ten in 1989.
Björk sang on their album ex:el, and Massey later co-wrote songs on her own records.

influencedBy.why: 808 State's early records grew straight out of the acid sound.
Detroit techno was part of the template they brought to Manchester.

cousins.why: Manchester's rave-era crossover between clubs and bands.
Madchester guitar music shaped by the same club scene.

artists.name: The Orb
artists.summary: Alex Paterson's project that slowed house music down into ambient house for chill-out rooms. Their early albums mix dub bass, samples and long, drifting tracks.
know: Paterson started the group with Jimmy Cauty of The KLF.

They made Metallic Spheres with David Gilmour in 2010 and an album with Lee Scratch Perry in 2012.

songs: A Huge Ever Growing Pulsating Brain That Rules from the Centre of the Ultraworld

influencedBy.why: The Orb's long ambient journeys draw on Tangerine Dream's 1970s records.

Their deep bass and echo come straight from dub.
They recorded an album with Perry and draw on his dub production.
Their spacey, long-form records nod clearly to Pink Floyd.
Jimmy Cauty was a founding member.
Ambient house borrowed the echo and drift of 1970s dub.

cousins.why: Dub production that brings reggae sound into other genres.
Slow, hypnotic music built for drifting.

artists.name: The KLF
artists.summary: Bill Drummond and Jimmy Cauty's prankish dance duo who made huge hits and then quit the music business. Their album Chill Out is also a landmark of ambient music.

Country singer Tammy Wynette sang on their hit Justified and Ancient.
They deleted their whole catalogue when they left music in 1992.

influencedBy.why: Chill Out follows the ambient path Eno set out.
Their early pure trance records grew out of acid house.
Cauty worked on The Orb's early ambient sessions, which fed into Chill Out.

cousins.why: A band that treated the music business as part of the art.
The country star whose voice anchored Justified and Ancient.

artists.name: Orbital
artists.summary: Brothers Phil and Paul Hartnoll, who made melodic techno that worked both in clubs and at rock festivals. Their live sets helped bring dance music to the main stage.
know: They named the band after the M25 orbital motorway that ringed the London raves.
Their first single Chime was recorded at home onto cassette.
Their 1994 Glastonbury set is often called a turning point for dance acts at festivals.

influencedBy.why: Orbital built their live shows around a version of her Doctor Who theme and have credited the Radiophonic Workshop.
Kraftwerk's melodic machine music is a core reference.
Detroit techno's emotional melodies shaped their sound.
Acid house was the music that started them making tracks.

cousins.why: Long instrumental pieces that build to big climaxes.
Instrumental music with political undertones and slow builds.

artists.name: Underworld
artists.summary: Karl Hyde and Rick Smith's group, which mixed techno with Hyde's stream-of-consciousness vocals. Born Slippy .NUXX became a defining song of 1990s British dance music.
know: DJ Darren Emerson joined in 1990 and shaped their club sound.
Born Slippy .NUXX was a hit after it appeared in the film Trainspotting.
They were music directors for the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.
keyAlbums: Barbara Barbara, We Face a Shining Future

influencedBy.why: Kraftwerk's steady pulse runs through their long tracks.

cousins.why: Rock that moved toward electronic textures and fragmented vocals.
Long, building instrumental pieces.

artists.name: Leftfield
artists.summary: Neil Barnes and Paul Daley's London duo, who blended house with heavy dub bass. Their album Leftism is one of the key British dance albums of the 1990s.
know: Leftism was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize in 1995.
John Lydon sang on their single Open Up.
Phat Planet was used in a well-known Guinness television advert.

influencedBy.why: PiL's dub-heavy bass shaped their sound, and Lydon sang on Open Up.
Their bass weight and echo come from dub.

cousins.why: Dub production applied across genres.
British rock that crossed into dance and dub.

artists.name: Goldie
artists.summary: A former graffiti artist who helped turn jungle into the more ambitious drum and bass. His album Timeless brought the genre to a wide audience.
know: He was known for graffiti art before he made records.

Inner City Life features singer Diane Charlemagne.

Jungle DJs sped up Bug in the Bassbin, and its breakbeat jazz fed early drum and bass.
Hip hop and b-boy culture shaped him as a graffiti writer and producer.

British street music made from fast, hard beats.

artists.name: Roni Size
artists.summary: A Bristol producer who led the collective Reprazent and brought live bass and jazz into drum and bass. New Forms won the Mercury Prize in 1997.
know: New Forms beat a shortlist that included Radiohead's OK Computer.
Reprazent included Krust, DJ Die, Suv, singer Onallee and MC Dynamite.

influencedBy.why: Bristol's sound-system culture around Massive Attack shaped his start.
Goldie's Timeless showed drum and bass could be an album form.

cousins.why: A live band playing beat-driven music.
Jazz with heavy, rolling bass at its centre.

artists.name: Tricky
artists.summary: A Bristol rapper and producer who appeared on Massive Attack's early records before making the dark, claustrophobic Maxinquaye. He is one of the defining voices of trip hop.

Black Steel is a reworking of Public Enemy's Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos.

Hell Is Round the Corner is built on a sample of Hayes's Ike's Rap II.

Murky, low-voiced rap built on hazy loops.

artists.name: Moby

Play uses vocals from Alan Lomax's field recordings on songs like Natural Blues.

A producer known for mashing up old records into something new.

artists.name: Fatboy Slim
artists.summary: Norman Cook's big beat project, built on breakbeats, rock riffs and catchy samples. Songs like The Rockafeller Skank and Praise You made him one of the biggest DJs of the late 1990s.

artists.name: Basement Jaxx

cousins.why: Genre-hopping dance-pop production.
Playful, colourful records that mix many styles.

artists.name: Autechre
artists.summary: Rob Brown and Sean Booth's duo, who started from electro and hip hop and moved into some of the most abstract electronic music on record. They are central to the Warp Records sound.

Detroit techno's melodies shaped their early records.

cousins.why: Rhythmically complex instrumental music.
Heavy music built on shifting, hard-to-count rhythm.

artists.name: Boards of Canada

artists.name: Squarepusher

artists.name: Air

Li Saumet's vocals draw on rap, dancehall and coastal Colombian styles.
Deja in 2021 was nominated for a Grammy.

influencedBy.why: Bomba Estéreo's mix of Latin folk rhythm and electronic and punk energy follows the mestizo sound.

cousins.why: Electronic producer drawing on global club rhythms.
Electronic music with a warm, organic pulse.

artists.name: King Sunny Adé
artists.summary: Nigerian guitarist and bandleader who modernized jùjú with layered guitars, pedal steel and synthesizers. Island Records released his music worldwide in the early 1980s, making him one of the first African stars of the world music boom.
know: He led the African Beats, a large band with several guitars and talking drums.
Island Records released Juju Music in 1982.
He added pedal steel guitar and synthesizers to jùjú.

cousins.why: Island Records promoted him as its next global star after Marley.
Interlocking guitars and drums in a deep groove.

artists.name: Tony Allen
artists.summary: Nigerian drummer who co-created Afrobeat as Fela Kuti's drummer and musical director. Fela said Afrobeat would not exist without him, and he later worked with Damon Albarn, Flea and Jeff Mills.
know: He played drums in Fela's Africa 70 from the late 1960s until 1979.
He taught himself drums partly by studying Art Blakey and Max Roach records.
His final album, Rejoice, was made with Hugh Masekela and released in 2020.

influencedBy.why: He has said Blakey's drumming was a central model when he taught himself.
He studied Roach's playing as he developed his own style.
Fela was his bandleader and partner in building Afrobeat.
Afrobeat's tight funk grooves draw on the James Brown band.

cousins.why: Deep, loose funk drumming at the center of a sound.
A band built on tight, interlocking funk.

artists.name: Franco & TPOK Jazz
artists.summary: Congolese band led by guitarist Franco Luambo Makiadi that was the dominant force in African popular music for three decades. TPOK Jazz built Congolese rumba from Cuban son and local rhythm.
know: Franco co-founded OK Jazz in Kinshasa in 1956.
The band often had dozens of members, with multiple singers and guitarists.
Franco's guitar style earned him the nickname 'the Sorcerer of the Guitar.'

influencedBy.why: Cuban son records like Arsenio's were heard widely in Congo and shaped Congolese rumba.
The Cuban big-band singing of Moré's era fed the rumba style.

cousins.why: A long-running big band led by a strong musical voice.
A bandleader who kept a huge, tight band at peak form.

artists.name: Miriam Makeba
artists.summary: South African singer known as 'Mama Africa' who brought South African music to the world. Her hit Pata Pata and her work with Harry Belafonte made her an international star.
know: She sang with the Manhattan Brothers and the Skylarks in the 1950s.
Harry Belafonte helped bring her to the United States in 1959.
An Evening with Belafonte/Makeba won the 1966 Grammy for Best Folk Recording.

influencedBy.why: Belafonte was her mentor in the US and recorded a Grammy-winning album with her.
Masekela was her husband and collaborator in the 1960s.

cousins.why: A singer whose music carried a strong message.
A powerful voice who stood for more than music.

artists.name: Hugh Masekela
artists.summary: South African trumpeter, flugelhornist and singer who carried township jazz and mbaqanga to international audiences. His 1968 instrumental Grazing in the Grass topped the US pop chart.
know: His first trumpet came from anti-apartheid priest Trevor Huddleston, who later arranged a gift horn from Louis Armstrong for the band Masekela played in.
He played in the Jazz Epistles, the first Black South African jazz group to record an LP.
He played trumpet on The Byrds' So You Want to Be a Rock 'n' Roll Star and appeared at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967.
keyAlbums: Home Is Where the Music Is

influencedBy.why: They made the album Rejoice together.
Armstrong was his first trumpet hero, and the gifted Armstrong horn tied the two together early.
Gillespie befriended and encouraged him when he arrived in New York and urged him to build on South African sounds.
His early bebop playing and later flugelhorn tone owed a clear debt to Davis.
Makeba, his wife in the mid 1960s and lifelong collaborator, helped him launch his American career.
Time with Fela and the West African scene pushed him toward the Afro-rock and highlife grooves of his Hedzoleh Soundz period.
Belafonte helped Masekela come to the US and start his career there.

cousins.why: Jazz that kept reaching toward funk and wider audiences.
Big, warm horn music built on jazz but aimed at a wide audience.
Jazz-rooted protest music with a deep groove.

artists.name: Ladysmith Black Mambazo
artists.summary: Male choral group founded by Joseph Shabalala that made the soft-stepping isicathamiya style famous worldwide. Their work on Paul Simon's Graceland led to a global career and several Grammy Awards.
know: Joseph Shabalala said the group's harmonies came to him in a series of dreams in 1964.
Their 1973 album Amabutho is often cited as the first gold record by Black South African musicians.
Shaka Zulu (1987), produced by Paul Simon, won the Grammy for Best Traditional Folk Recording.
songs: Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes

cousins.why: Tight, rhythmic male vocal harmony rooted in sacred music.
Gospel quartet singing where blended voices carry everything.
Polished a cappella quartet work with deep bass and high leads.

artists.name: Youssou N'Dour
artists.summary: Senegalese singer and bandleader who built mbalax, a fusion of sabar drumming, griot singing and Afro-Cuban and pop elements, into one of Africa's best known sounds. He is among the most famous voices to come out of West Africa.
know: He led the Étoile de Dakar and then the Super Étoile de Dakar, the bands that defined mbalax.
His album Egypt won the Grammy for Best Contemporary World Music Album in 2005.
He served as Senegal's Minister of Culture and Tourism from 2012 to 2013.

influencedBy.why: Brought him onto In Your Eyes and the So tour, introducing him to rock audiences.

cousins.why: A national voice who turned a local rhythm into a global one.
Commanding singer at the front of a hard-driving dance band.

artists.name: Salif Keita
artists.summary: Malian singer known as the Golden Voice of Africa, who came up in the Rail Band and Les Ambassadeurs before a solo career that mixed Mande griot singing with funk, jazz and synthesizers.
know: He is a descendant of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire.
His breakthrough solo album Soro (1987) was recorded in Paris and set Mande melodies to modern production.
Amen (1991) was produced by Joe Zawinul and featured Wayne Shorter and Carlos Santana.

influencedBy.why: Weather Report keyboardist Joe Zawinul produced Amen and shaped its jazz-fusion sheen.
Carlos Santana played on Amen, adding Latin-rock guitar to his sound.

cousins.why: A huge, soaring voice that carries sacred intensity.
A singer whose voice alone can hold a whole song.

artists.name: Ali Farka Touré
artists.summary: Malian guitarist and singer whose hypnotic, modal playing drew a direct line between West African music and American blues. His records with Ry Cooder and Toumani Diabaté won Grammy Awards.
know: Talking Timbuktu, made with Ry Cooder, won the Grammy for Best World Music Album in 1995.
In the Heart of the Moon, with kora player Toumani Diabaté, won the same award in 2006.
He became mayor of his hometown Niafunké in 2004 and spent much of his time farming there.

influencedBy.why: He said hearing Hooker convinced him the blues had African roots, and his drones are often compared to Hooker's.

cousins.why: Spare, rolling acoustic blues full of space.
Hill country blues built on repeating hypnotic riffs.

artists.name: Tinariwen
artists.summary: Tuareg collective founded by Ibrahim Ag Alhabib whose rolling electric guitars and call-and-response vocals brought Saharan music to rock audiences. Their success sparked a wave of desert guitar bands.
know: Ibrahim Ag Alhabib built his first guitar as a boy from a tin can, a stick and bicycle wire.
Their international debut, The Radio Tisdas Sessions, came out in 2001 after the band played the first Festival au Désert.
Tassili, recorded acoustically in the Algerian desert with guests from TV on the Radio and Wilco's Nels Cline, won the 2012 Grammy for Best World Music Album.

influencedBy.why: His international success opened the door for Saharan guitar bands, and Tinariwen's sound follows his modal blues.

cousins.why: Droning, hypnotic guitar blues that locks into one groove.
Trance-like boogie built on a single riff.
Long, rolling guitar music made for driving across open space.

artists.name: Mulatu Astatke
artists.summary: Vibraphonist, percussionist and arranger known as the father of Ethio-jazz, who joined Ethiopian scales to jazz and Latin rhythms. His records found a new global audience through the Éthiopiques series and film soundtracks.
know: He was the first African student at Berklee College of Music.
He arranged and played with Duke Ellington's orchestra during Ellington's 1973 visit to Ethiopia.
Jim Jarmusch built the soundtrack of Broken Flowers (2005) around his music.

influencedBy.why: He studied Ellington's orchestration and later worked with his band in Addis Ababa.
His New York years in the Latin jazz scene led to the mambo and boogaloo feel of Afro-Latin Soul.
Modal jazz showed him how to set long improvisations over Ethiopian scales.

cousins.why: Jazz bandleader who reached for sounds and scales far outside the standard.
Bold Latin jazz with adventurous harmony.
Jazz that leans hard into groove and texture.

artists.name: Angélique Kidjo
artists.summary: Beninese singer and songwriter who mixes West African rhythms with funk, jazz and pop. She is one of the most decorated African artists at the Grammy Awards.
know: She moved to Paris in 1983, where she studied jazz and launched her international career.
Her 2018 album Remain in Light reworked the whole Talking Heads record with African arrangements.
She has won five Grammy Awards and is a long-serving UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

influencedBy.why: Kidjo has named Makeba as her idol and later recorded a tribute to her.
Brown's funk records were a teenage obsession and shape her rhythm sections.
She remade Remain in Light song by song, tracing its African roots.
She paid tribute with the 2019 album Celia, honoring Cruz's Afro-Cuban music.
Afrobeat's horn-driven grooves run through her funkiest work.
Franklin's soul singing was a key model for her vocal power.

cousins.why: A powerhouse voice fronting heavy funk.
A singer who became the voice of a whole continent.

artists.name: Wizkid
artists.summary: Nigerian singer from Surulere, Lagos, who became one of the faces of the global Afrobeats boom. His Made in Lagos album and the hit Essence pushed Nigerian pop into the US mainstream.
know: He broke through on Banky W's label Empire Mates Entertainment with Holla at Your Boy in 2010.
He sang on Drake's One Dance, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 2016.
The Essence remix with Justin Bieber reached the Hot 100 top 10, a first for a Nigerian song.

influencedBy.why: He has named Fela as a hero, and Afrobeat's groove sits under his mid-tempo style.
He often cites Marley, and reggae's easy sway runs through his records.
Sponono also brought Wizkid into the amapiano sound.

cousins.why: The biggest star of a non-English pop wave that conquered US charts.
Island dance music that crossed over without losing its accent.

artists.name: Davido
artists.summary: Atlanta-born, Lagos-raised singer and producer whose upbeat party hits made him one of Nigeria's biggest stars. His song Fall became one of the longest-charting Nigerian songs in the US.
know: His breakout single Dami Duro came out in 2011, and he produced much of his early work himself.
Fall (2017) was certified gold in the United States.
His album Timeless (2023) earned him multiple Grammy nominations.

influencedBy.why: Fela's Afrobeat is the foundation of the Nigerian pop he grew up with.

cousins.why: The party-starting voice of a dance-pop movement that went global.
Feel-good dancehall pop built for clubs and radio.

artists.name: Tems
artists.summary: Nigerian singer, songwriter and producer with a low, smoky voice who became a major figure in global R&B after Wizkid's Essence. She has written and sung on Grammy-winning and Oscar-nominated songs.
know: She taught herself to produce and released her first single, Mr Rebel, in 2018.
Future's Wait for U, built on her song Higher and featuring her vocals, won a Grammy in 2023.
Love Me JeJe won the Grammy for Best African Music Performance in 2025.

influencedBy.why: Essence, built around their duet, made Tems a global name.
She has named Hill as a key influence on her mix of singing, writing and conviction.
Her unhurried, jazzy phrasing follows the neo-soul path Badu opened.

cousins.why: Moody, conversational modern R&B.
A warm, understated voice over spare soul production.

artists.name: Rema
artists.summary: Nigerian singer who calls his sound Afrorave, mixing Afrobeats with trap and Indian and Arabic melodic touches. His song Calm Down became one of the biggest African hits ever.
know: He signed to Don Jazzy's Mavin Records in 2019, and his song Iron Man appeared on Barack Obama's summer playlist that year.
The Calm Down remix with Selena Gomez reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Calm Down became the first song by an African artist to pass one billion streams on Spotify.

influencedBy.why: Wizkid's smooth crossover Afropop was the model his generation of Nigerian singers grew up on.

cousins.why: Melodic, effects-heavy rap built for big rooms.
A genre-blending young star who made his local scene global.

artists.name: Tyla
artists.summary: South African singer who blends amapiano's log drums with R&B and pop. Her single Water made her a global star in 2023.
know: Water won the first Grammy for Best African Music Performance in 2024.
Water made her the first South African solo artist on the Billboard Hot 100 since Hugh Masekela in the 1960s.
She calls her sound popiano, a mix of pop and amapiano.

influencedBy.why: When Water charted in the US in 2023, she became the first South African solo act on the Hot 100 since his 1968 run.
She has named Rihanna as a model for blending island roots with global pop.
She often cites Aaliyah, and her airy R&B vocals follow that style.
She has named Jackson as a reason she wanted to perform.
Amapiano's log-drum sound, which Kabza De Small helped define, is the base of her records.

cousins.why: Dance-forward R&B pop led by choreography and groove.
Silky R&B that mixes in rhythms from home.

artists.name: Kabza De Small
artists.summary: South African DJ and producer widely called the King of Amapiano, whose huge output helped turn the Pretoria and Johannesburg township sound into a continental movement.
know: He formed the duo Scorpion Kings with DJ Maphorisa.
His 2020 album I Am the King of Amapiano: Sweet & Dust set streaming records in South Africa.
Sponono, with DJ Maphorisa, brought Wizkid and Burna Boy onto an amapiano track.
keyAlbums: I Am the King of Amapiano: Sweet & Dust
Rumble in the Jungle (Scorpion Kings with Tresor)

influencedBy.why: South African deep house, led by Black Coffee, is the sound amapiano grew out of.

cousins.why: Warm, patient house music made for long DJ sets.
A producer with a signature swing that crossed into pop.

artists.name: Black Coffee
artists.summary: South African DJ and producer who took Afro house from Durban to the world's biggest clubs. His album Subconsciously won a Grammy.
know: Subconsciously won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album in 2022.
He held a long-running weekly residency in Ibiza.
He co-produced Get It Together on Drake's More Life and worked on Drake's Honestly, Nevermind.

influencedBy.why: Chicago house set the soulful, steady template for his DJ style.
Heard's deep, melodic house is the direct ancestor of his sound.

cousins.why: Warm, organic electronic music that travels well.
A DJ who brought deep house to a global pop audience.

artists.name: Seo Taiji and Boys
artists.summary: Trio of Seo Taiji, Yang Hyun-suk and Lee Juno whose rap, dance and rock hybrid broke the ballad-heavy mold of Korean pop. They are widely credited as the starting point of modern K-pop.
know: They debuted on a TV talent show in 1992, got the lowest score from the judges, and their song Nan Arayo then topped the charts for weeks.
Seo Taiji had played bass in the heavy metal band Sinawe before forming the group.
Member Yang Hyun-suk went on to found YG Entertainment, home of Big Bang and Blackpink.

influencedBy.why: Their debut leaned on the new jack swing beats Riley pioneered.
Come Back Home borrowed the heavy, hazy West Coast rap sound of Cypress Hill.
Seo Taiji's metal background shows in the hard guitars of their later albums.

cousins.why: Rap that freely mixed in rock guitars and attitude.
A group that set the template for an entire wave of pop acts.

artists.name: Big Bang
artists.summary: YG Entertainment boy group led by G-Dragon, who wrote and produced much of their music. Their hip-hop and electronic hits made them one of the most influential K-pop acts of their era.
know: Their 2007 single Lies, co-written by G-Dragon, was their breakthrough hit in Korea.
Fantastic Baby (2012) became one of the best known K-pop songs outside Asia.
Bang Bang Bang won Song of the Year at the 2015 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

influencedBy.why: Yang Hyun-suk built YG Entertainment, and Big Bang, on the hip-hop idol model the trio created.
G-Dragon has cited Pharrell Williams, and the Neptunes' bright, minimal beats show up in their work.
Their mix of rap swagger and electronic pop follows the late 2000s Kanye sound.

cousins.why: A boy band that took creative control of its own songs.
The defining boy band of an earlier pop generation.

artists.name: Psy
artists.summary: South Korean rapper, singer and producer known for comic, high-energy dance songs. Gangnam Style made him the first viral global K-pop star.
know: Gangnam Style was the first YouTube video to reach one billion views, in December 2012.
He studied in the United States at Boston University and Berklee College of Music.
He signed with YG Entertainment in 2010, two years before Gangnam Style.

influencedBy.why: Psy signed to YG and grew out of the Korean rap-pop scene the trio started.
He has said seeing a Queen concert video made him want to be a performer.

cousins.why: Pop built on humor and over-the-top videos.
A viral novelty hit that turned into a real career.

artists.name: BTS
artists.summary: Seven-member group from Big Hit Entertainment that started as a hip-hop crew and became the best-selling act in K-pop history. They took Korean pop to the top of the US charts.
know: Love Yourself: Tear (2018) was the first K-pop album to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
Dynamite (2020) was the first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 by a South Korean act.
Leader RM spoke at the United Nations General Assembly in 2018.

influencedBy.why: BTS covered Come Back Home in 2017 and performed with Seo Taiji at his 25th anniversary concert.
RM has named Nas as one of the rappers who got him into hip-hop.
RM and Suga have cited Eminem as a formative rap influence.

cousins.why: The biggest boy band of the same decade, with a huge fan base.
A vocal group that defined pop for its era.

artists.name: Blackpink
artists.summary: YG Entertainment girl group of Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé and Lisa, whose loud, drop-heavy singles made them the most popular K-pop girl group worldwide.
know: Most of their hits were produced by YG's in-house producer Teddy Park.
They were the first K-pop girl group to play Coachella, in 2019, and they headlined it in 2023.
Born Pink (2022) was the first album by a female K-pop group to top the Billboard 200.

influencedBy.why: Blackpink came out of YG, the company founded by member Yang Hyun-suk.
Blackpink were built by the same YG team as a female counterpart to Big Bang.
BLACKPINK's distinct-member girl group format follows the Spice Girls blueprint.

cousins.why: A girl group with distinct personalities that went global.
A vocal group that defined pop for its decade.

artists.name: NewJeans
artists.summary: Five-member group created by Min Hee-jin at ADOR whose soft vocals and breakbeat, Jersey club and late 1990s R&B touches moved K-pop away from loud maximalism.
know: Their debut single Attention and the song Hype Boy came out together in 2022 with no pre-release teasers.
Super Shy and ETA used fast Jersey club drum patterns, produced with 250 and others.
Their EP Get Up reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in 2023.

influencedBy.why: Their breezy late 1990s girl group R&B feel follows TLC and their peers.
The smooth group harmonies and R&B swing recall 1990s acts like SWV.

cousins.why: Light, breathy vocals over fast breakbeats and garage drums.
Cool, understated R&B singing over inventive beats.

artists.name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
artists.summary: Composer, pianist and producer who co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra and went on to an Oscar-winning film career and decades of ambient and experimental work.
know: He co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra with Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi in 1978.
He shared the Academy Award for Best Original Score for The Last Emperor.
His 1980 track Riot in Lagos is often cited as an early blueprint for electro.

influencedBy.why: Hosono invited him into YMO and was his main creative partner in the band.
Kraftwerk's machine pop was a direct model for YMO and his early synth records.
Eno's ambient approach is a clear ancestor of his later minimal work.

cousins.why: Synthesizer music that moved easily between pop and film.
Electronic music that moves between beats and quiet ambient pieces.

artists.name: Happy End
artists.summary: Band of Haruomi Hosono, Eiichi Ohtaki, Shigeru Suzuki and Takashi Matsumoto that proved rock could be sung in Japanese. Its members went on to shape city pop, YMO and decades of Japanese pop.
know: Their choice to sing rock in Japanese, not English, set off a famous debate in the Japanese music press.
Kaze o Atsumete was used in the 2003 film Lost in Translation.
Their final album was recorded in Los Angeles with Van Dyke Parks producing.
songs: Juuni Gatsu no Ame no Hi

influencedBy.why: Their guitar-led folk rock was openly modeled on Buffalo Springfield.
The jangling folk rock of The Byrds shaped their early sound.
Their rootsy, ensemble feel shows a debt to The Band.

cousins.why: Harmony-rich folk rock made by future stars.
A short-lived band whose influence grew huge after it ended.

artists.name: Tatsuro Yamashita
artists.summary: Singer, guitarist and producer who became the defining voice of Japanese city pop, known for lush harmonies and tight funk grooves. His records found a big new overseas audience online in the 2010s.
know: He started in the band Sugar Babe, whose debut was produced by Eiichi Ohtaki of Happy End.
Christmas Eve (1983) has returned to the Japanese charts nearly every winter for decades.
He produced and arranged his wife Mariya Takeuchi's records, including Plastic Love.

influencedBy.why: Eiichi Ohtaki signed Yamashita's band Sugar Babe to his Niagara label and produced their debut.
He has said the Beach Boys' harmonies shaped his vocal arranging, and Big Wave covers their songs.
He adored Spector's dense wall of sound records.
The blue-eyed soul of The Young Rascals is a stated favorite.
His funk guitar and smooth soul arrangements draw on Mayfield's records.

cousins.why: Glossy, jazzy studio pop with session-player precision.
Smooth, harmony-driven soft rock with funk underneath.
Bright horns, tight grooves and big vocal blends.

artists.name: Haruomi Hosono
artists.summary: Bassist, songwriter and producer who played in Happy End, made a run of exotica-flavored solo records, and then founded Yellow Magic Orchestra. He is one of the central figures in Japanese pop.
know: He was the bassist and a main songwriter in Happy End.
His mid 1970s albums Tropical Dandy and Bon Voyage co. mixed exotica, Okinawan music and New Orleans rhythm.
He formed YMO in 1978 after inviting Ryuichi Sakamoto and Yukihiro Takahashi to work on a cover of Martin Denny's Firecracker.

influencedBy.why: The band was where Hosono first developed as a songwriter and bassist.
Buffalo Springfield was the template for his early folk rock with Happy End.
Hosono House's loose, homemade sound follows The Band.
Little Feat's New Orleans-flavored grooves fed into his Tropical Dandy period.
Kraftwerk showed him how pop could be built from machines, leading to YMO.

cousins.why: A restless studio musician who moved from rock to electronic and ambient.
A pop craftsman and producer who kept switching styles.

artists.name: X Japan
artists.summary: Band led by drummer, pianist and composer Yoshiki that mixed speed metal with classical piano and huge ballads. They are credited as founders of the visual kei movement.
know: Yoshiki and singer Toshi formed the band as childhood friends in Tateyama, Chiba.
Blue Blood (1989) made them stars, and Jealousy (1991) topped the Oricon chart.
Art of Life (1993) is a single song nearly half an hour long.

influencedBy.why: Yoshiki has said seeing Kiss made him want to play rock, and their makeup and staging fed visual kei.
Their galloping twin-guitar speed metal follows the British metal of Iron Maiden.
Judas Priest's high-pitched, fast metal is a clear ancestor of their sound.
Their mix of rock and grand, operatic ballads echoes Queen.

cousins.why: Long, technically dazzling metal with classical ambition.
Big hooks, power ballads and arena-sized metal.

artists.name: Boredoms
artists.summary: Osaka band led by Yamantaka Eye that went from chaotic noise rock to long, drum-heavy psychedelic trance pieces. They became a cult touchstone for American indie and experimental bands.
know: They toured with Sonic Youth and Nirvana and played Lollapalooza in 1994.
Super Ae and Vision Creation Newsun traded noise for huge, looping rhythmic builds.
On July 7, 2007, they staged 77 Boadrum in Brooklyn with 77 drummers playing together.

influencedBy.why: Their early cut-up, absurd noise rock owes a lot to the Butthole Surfers.
Their long, locked-in trance rhythms follow Can's approach.
The driving, repeating pulse of their late 1990s work recalls Neu!

cousins.why: Heavy, noisy and unpredictable underground rock.
Cosmic, ritual-like music with a huge drum section.

artists.name: Utada Hikaru
artists.summary: Singer, songwriter and producer raised between Tokyo and New York whose R&B-inflected debut became the best-selling album in Japanese history. She writes and produces her own music.
know: Her debut album First Love (1999) sold more than seven million copies in Japan.
She wrote and sang Simple and Clean and Hikari for the Kingdom Hearts video games.
Her mother was the famous enka singer Keiko Fuji.

influencedBy.why: Her debut brought the late 1990s US R&B sound of singers like Blige into J-pop.
The crisp, syncopated R&B production of the late 1990s shaped Automatic.

cousins.why: Cool, understated R&B singing over inventive production.
A pop artist who took control of her own sound and grew more adventurous.

artists.name: Babymetal
artists.summary: Group that fuses Japanese idol pop vocals and choreography with heavy metal backing. They became one of the most successful Japanese acts abroad.
know: They started as a sub-unit of the idol group Sakura Gakuin.
Metal Resistance (2016) reached No. 39 on the Billboard 200, the best showing by a Japanese act in decades.
They opened shows for Lady Gaga, Metallica and Red Hot Chili Peppers.

influencedBy.why: Their mix of speed metal and Japanese spectacle follows the path X Japan opened.
Their backing band's thrash riffs are rooted in Metallica-style metal.

cousins.why: Modern metal that happily mixes in pop and electronic sounds.
A gleeful collision of cute pop and heavy noise.

artists.name: Yoasobi
artists.summary: Duo of producer Ayase and singer Ikura who turn short stories into fast, intricate pop songs. Their anime theme Idol became a global chart hit.
know: Each of their early songs adapted a short story posted on the writing site Monogatary.com.
Ayase started out as a Vocaloid producer before forming the duo.
Idol, the theme for Oshi no Ko, topped the Billboard Global Excl. US chart in 2023, a first for a Japanese song.

cousins.why: Anime-inspired electronic pop full of bright, emotional melodies.
Exact, melody-packed pop that rewards repeat listening.

artists.name: R.D. Burman
artists.summary: Composer known as Pancham who brought rock, funk, Latin and disco sounds into Hindi film music in the 1960s and 1970s. His scores remain among the most sampled and loved in Bollywood.
know: He was the son of the composer S.D. Burman and worked as his father's assistant before scoring on his own.
He was known for found sounds, such as blowing across bottles and rubbing comb and paper, in his arrangements.
He married singer Asha Bhosle, who sang many of his biggest songs, in 1980.

influencedBy.why: Latin big band rhythms like Prado's mambo show up all over his 1960s scores.
Western rock and roll fed the guitar-driven songs of Teesri Manzil.

cousins.why: A composer with sophisticated, instantly hummable arrangements.
A genre-crossing arranger with an ear for groove.
Bright, Latin-tinged pop orchestration.

artists.name: Lata Mangeshkar
artists.summary: Playback singer known as the Nightingale of India whose voice defined Hindi film song for more than half a century. She recorded in dozens of Indian languages.
know: Her breakthrough came with Aayega Aanewala from the 1949 film Mahal.
She received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor, in 2001.
She was the elder sister of singer Asha Bhosle.

cousins.why: A pure, flawless voice that defined a whole songbook.
A singer whose voice became the sound of a genre.

artists.name: Asha Bhosle
artists.summary: Playback singer with a huge range who sang everything from ghazals to cabaret and disco in Hindi film. She is one of the most recorded singers in history.
know: Guinness World Records recognized her in 2011 as the most recorded artist in music history.
Her partnership with R.D. Burman produced many of the boldest Bollywood songs of the 1970s.

A composer of lush, intricate arrangements for popular song.

artists.name: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan

artists.name: Umm Kulthum

A singer who became the voice of a whole region.

artists.name: Soft Machine
artists.summary: Soft Machine was the founding band of the Canterbury scene, moving from psychedelic pop to long, jazz-based instrumental pieces. They were among the first British rock bands to fully embrace jazz improvisation.
know: Early members included Robert Wyatt, Kevin Ayers, Mike Ratledge and Daevid Allen.
They supported the Jimi Hendrix Experience on its 1968 North American tour.
Third is a double album made of four side-long pieces.

influencedBy.why: Their turn to electric jazz around Third followed the same direction as Miles Davis.
Long modal improvisation in their instrumentals draws on Coltrane.
Free jazz shaped Elton Dean's and Ratledge's more open playing.
Their first psychedelic pop songs grew out of the Beatles era.

cousins.why: Electric jazz built on long group pieces.
Instrumental rock that borrows jazz structure.

artists.name: Caravan
artists.summary: Caravan is a Canterbury band known for gentle, whimsical songs that open into long jazz-flavored instrumental passages. In the Land of Grey and Pink is a defining record of the scene.
know: The band formed from the Wilde Flowers with Pye Hastings, Richard and David Sinclair and Richard Coughlan.
Nine Feet Underground fills a whole side of In the Land of Grey and Pink.
Richard Sinclair later joined Camel.
keyAlbums: If I Could Do It All Over Again, I'd Do It All Over You
In the Land of Grey and Pink
For Girls Who Grow Plump in the Night
songs: In the Land of Grey and Pink

influencedBy.why: Caravan came out of the same Wilde Flowers circle and shared players and ideas.
Their melodic, quirky English songwriting draws on 1960s Beatles pop.
Early Pink Floyd's whimsical English psychedelia fed Caravan's sound.

cousins.why: Soft English voice with quiet, pastoral songwriting.
Gentle, whimsical keyboard-led melody.

artists.name: Procol Harum
artists.summary: Procol Harum combined Gary Brooker's soulful piano and voice, Hammond organ and Keith Reid's lyrics into a stately, classical-tinged rock. Their debut single became one of the most played songs of the 1960s.
know: Lyricist Keith Reid was a full member of the band even though he did not perform.
A Whiter Shade of Pale borrows the feel of Bach's Air on the G String.
Organist Matthew Fisher won a share of the song's writing credit in a 2009 House of Lords ruling.

influencedBy.why: Gary Brooker's earlier band the Paramounts played R&B, and his gospel-soul singing comes from Ray Charles.
Keith Reid's surreal, literary lyrics follow Dylan's mid-1960s writing.
The band emerged in the post-Sgt. Pepper moment when pop took on classical color.

cousins.why: Hammond organ as the heart of the record.
A slow, organ-led soul ballad feel.

artists.name: The Moody Blues
artists.summary: The Moody Blues began as an R&B beat group and reinvented themselves as pioneers of orchestral, Mellotron-based rock. Days of Future Passed helped launch the idea of the rock concept album.
know: Their 1964 single Go Now, sung by Denny Laine, reached number one in the UK.
Days of Future Passed was recorded with the London Festival Orchestra.
Mike Pinder's Mellotron gave the band its sweeping string-like sound on stage.
keyAlbums: In Search of the Lost Chord
On the Threshold of a Dream
songs: I'm Just a Singer (In a Rock and Roll Band)

influencedBy.why: Produced The Other Side of Life and Sur la Mer.
Their move into lush studio concept records came in the wake of the Beatles' 1967 work.
They started in the same R&B beat-group scene as the Animals.
They began as an R&B beat group in the same scene the Stones led.

cousins.why: Lush, orchestral pop arrangements.
Grand, layered studio pop with a spiritual bent.

artists.name: Supertramp
artists.summary: Supertramp blended progressive rock structure with tight pop hooks, built around Wurlitzer electric piano and two contrasting songwriters. Breakfast in America made them one of the best-selling bands of the late 1970s.
know: Their early years were funded by Dutch patron Stanley August Miesegaes.
Rick Davies and Roger Hodgson wrote separately and sang their own songs in very different voices.
Breakfast in America won Grammys for Best Engineered Recording and Best Album Package.

influencedBy.why: Hodgson's bright, melodic songs follow the Beatles' pop craft.
Rick Davies's blues and R&B keyboard style traces back to Ray Charles.
Keyboard-led English art rock with strong melodies follows Procol Harum.

cousins.why: Piano-driven rock songs with big choruses.
Keyboard-led 1970s pop rock with art-rock touches.

artists.name: Kansas
artists.summary: Kansas brought British-style progressive rock to the American heartland, adding violin and boogie-rock power. Carry On Wayward Son and Dust in the Wind made them a fixture of classic rock radio.
know: Robbie Steinhardt's violin was a lead voice alongside guitars and keyboards.
Kerry Livgren wrote most of their best-known songs.
Dust in the Wind grew out of a fingerpicking exercise Livgren was practicing.

influencedBy.why: Kansas's keyboard-heavy American prog draws on ELP's style.
Kansas's long, multi-part pieces follow the symphonic prog of Yes.
Genesis's keyboard-driven writing shaped Kansas's mid-1970s albums.
King Crimson's heavy prog set an early model for the band.

cousins.why: Fiddle as a lead voice with clear, high vocals.
Virtuosic, genre-crossing playing rooted in American music.

artists.name: The Alan Parsons Project
artists.summary: The Alan Parsons Project paired Abbey Road engineer Alan Parsons with songwriter Eric Woolfson to make polished, concept-driven studio albums. Parsons's engineering on records by the Beatles and Pink Floyd set a high standard for rock sound.
know: Alan Parsons worked as an engineer on the Beatles' Abbey Road and Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon.
The Project used a rotating cast of guest singers instead of a fixed frontman.
The instrumental Sirius became a common arena intro, notably for the Chicago Bulls.
keyAlbums: The Dark Side of the Moon (Pink Floyd)
songs: (The System of) Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether
I Wouldn't Want to Be Like You

influencedBy.why: Parsons learned his craft as an assistant engineer on the Beatles' last sessions at Abbey Road.
Parsons worked under George Martin's production approach at Abbey Road.
Engineering Dark Side of the Moon shaped the Project's polished, conceptual sound.

cousins.why: Producer-led records built on studio polish.
Concept albums built around synthesizers and sound design.
Grand, cinematic studio music.

artists.name: Mike Oldfield
artists.summary: Mike Oldfield is an English multi-instrumentalist best known for Tubular Bells, a long instrumental piece he built almost entirely by overdubbing himself. It launched Virgin Records and helped create the market for instrumental rock albums.
know: He played bass and guitar in Kevin Ayers's band the Whole World as a teenager.
Tubular Bells was the first album released on Virgin Records in 1973.
The opening of Tubular Bells became widely known after its use in the film The Exorcist.

influencedBy.why: Former Soft Machine member Kevin Ayers took Oldfield into his band and encouraged his early writing.
English folk rock fed the folk melodies and Celtic textures of Hergest Ridge and Ommadawn.
Oldfield's early folk guitar in the Sallyangie draws on Bert Jansch.

cousins.why: Long-form instrumental music built in the studio.
Instrumental albums that became mainstream hits.
Celtic melody in a modern, layered setting.

artists.name: Peter Gabriel
artists.summary: Peter Gabriel was the original singer of Genesis and then a solo artist who mixed art rock, soul and music from around the world. His 1980s records changed pop production and helped bring African and Asian musicians to wider audiences.
know: He left Genesis in 1975 after the tour for The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway.
His third solo album helped introduce the gated-reverb drum sound, recorded with Hugh Padgham and Phil Collins.
He co-founded the WOMAD festival in 1982 and later the Real World label and studios.

influencedBy.why: He sang the closing Wolof passage on Gabriel's In Your Eyes and toured with him in the late 1980s.
Gabriel featured him on Passion, his Last Temptation of Christ score, and signed him to Real World.
Co-produced So and Us.
Produced Peter Gabriel's first solo album.
Gabriel was Genesis's singer and a core writer for its first six albums.
Gabriel has named 1960s soul singers like Otis Redding as models, heard in Sledgehammer's horns.
The Beatles were a key early influence on his songwriting.

cousins.why: Art rock built on African and global rhythms.
Restless, studio-driven pop with strong visual ideas.

artists.name: Marillion
artists.summary: Marillion led the 1980s revival of progressive rock, first with the theatrical Fish and then with Steve Hogarth. They later pioneered fan-funded recording.
know: Singer Fish fronted the band until 1988, when Steve Hogarth took over.
Kayleigh reached number two in the UK in 1985.
Fans paid in advance to fund the making of Anoraknophobia, an early example of crowdfunding.

influencedBy.why: Marillion's melodic neo-prog guitar leads echo Latimer's style.
Fish has cited Hammill as a major influence on his theatrical singing.
Fish has named Gabriel's Genesis-era theater as a model for his own stage persona.
Marillion's early sound draws directly on Gabriel-era Genesis.
Steve Rothery's sustained guitar leads draw on David Gilmour.

cousins.why: Big, emotional 1980s songs with prog-sized ambition.
Atmospheric, emotional guitar music with long builds.

artists.name: Porcupine Tree
artists.summary: Porcupine Tree is Steven Wilson's band, which moved from psychedelic space rock to a sharper mix of prog, pop melody and metal weight. They became a central band of 2000s progressive rock.
know: The band began as a Steven Wilson solo project with an invented backstory.
Drummer Gavin Harrison joined in 2002 for In Absentia.
Wilson produced Opeth's Blackwater Park and later remixed many classic prog catalogs.

influencedBy.why: Steven Wilson's atmospheric instrumental passages draw on Camel-style melodic prog.
Their early space rock and long atmospheric pieces draw heavily on Pink Floyd.
Wilson has cited King Crimson as a core influence, and later remixed its catalog.
Wilson pointed to Meshuggah's heaviness when the band added metal weight on In Absentia.
The band's early synth-heavy ambient passages draw on Tangerine Dream.

cousins.why: Slow-building, atmospheric music with emotional weight.
Melancholy art rock that mixes rock and electronics.
Dark, layered studio atmosphere.

artists.name: Hawkwind
artists.summary: Hawkwind is the founding band of space rock, led by Dave Brock, built on droning riffs, electronic effects and science-fiction themes. Their raw, repetitive sound fed directly into punk and heavy metal.
know: Lemmy played bass with the band from 1971 to 1975 before forming Motorhead.
Silver Machine, sung by Lemmy, reached number three in the UK in 1972.
Science-fiction writer Michael Moorcock wrote and performed with the band.
keyAlbums: Warrior on the Edge of Time

influencedBy.why: Early Pink Floyd's space-themed psychedelia set the scene for Hawkwind.
Hawkwind's long, locked repetitive grooves share Can's approach.
Hendrix's feedback and effects pointed toward Hawkwind's electronic noise.

cousins.why: Cosmic themes and freeform, otherworldly sound.
Electronic space music built on long sequences.

artists.name: John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers
artists.summary: John Mayall's Bluesbreakers were the training ground of British blues, with a rotating lineup that launched many major guitarists and rhythm sections. Mayall's devotion to Chicago blues set the standard for the 1960s British blues boom.
know: Alumni include Eric Clapton, Peter Green, Mick Taylor, John McVie and Mick Fleetwood.
Blues Breakers with Eric Clapton, nicknamed the Beano album, made Clapton's loud Les Paul tone famous.
The Turning Point was recorded live with no drummer, using acoustic guitar, flute and saxophone.
songs: Have You Ever Loved a Woman

influencedBy.why: Korner encouraged Mayall to move to London and turn professional.
The band's version of Hideaway brought Freddie King's instrumental to British players.
Chicago West Side guitarists like Buddy Guy shaped the guitar style Mayall's players used.
Mayall's band followed the electric blues tradition T-Bone Walker started.

cousins.why: A bandleader whose group trained a generation of stars.
A rock-era band devoted to authentic Chicago blues.

artists.name: Alexis Korner
artists.summary: Alexis Korner was a guitarist, singer and bandleader often called the father of British blues. His band Blues Incorporated and his club nights gave many of the 1960s' biggest rock musicians their start.
know: He founded Blues Incorporated with harmonica player Cyril Davies in 1961.
Blues Incorporated's players and guests included Charlie Watts, Jack Bruce, Ginger Baker and Mick Jagger.
His big-band project CCS recorded the version of Whole Lotta Love used as the Top of the Pops theme.
songs: I Got My Brand on You

influencedBy.why: Muddy Waters's 1958 UK tour with electric guitar pushed Korner toward amplified Chicago blues.
Broonzy's British visits in the 1950s were a key early influence on Korner.
Korner came up through the skiffle and folk-blues scene built on Lead Belly's songs.

cousins.why: A British bandleader who turned American roots music into a homegrown movement.
A champion who spread the blues to new audiences.

artists.name: Ten Years After
artists.summary: Ten Years After is a British blues rock band led for its classic years by fast-fingered guitarist Alvin Lee. Their Woodstock performance made them one of the defining live acts of the era.
know: Alvin Lee's speed on the guitar made him one of the most talked-about players of the late 1960s.
Their version of I'm Going Home at Woodstock was a highlight of the 1970 concert film.
I'd Love to Change the World was a US hit in 1971.
songs: I'd Love to Change the World

influencedBy.why: Alvin Lee's rock and roll guitar runs come straight from Chuck Berry.
Their boogie grooves draw on John Lee Hooker.
The band's blues base is Chicago electric blues.

cousins.why: Fast, fiery blues guitar at the center of the show.
Speed and power in modern electric blues guitar.

artists.name: Savoy Brown
artists.summary: Savoy Brown was a British blues rock band led by guitarist Kim Simmonds for nearly six decades. They found their biggest audience touring the United States with heavy boogie blues.
know: Kim Simmonds led the band through many lineups from its start until 2022.
Three members left in 1970 and formed the band Foghat.
The band was more popular in the US than in Britain.

influencedBy.why: Savoy Brown's set leaned on Chicago blues songs like Louisiana Blues.
Their long boogie jams follow Hooker's one-chord drive.
They rose in the London blues scene Mayall's band led.

cousins.why: Hypnotic, repetitive boogie blues.
Gritty, riff-driven blues rock.

artists.name: Rory Gallagher
artists.summary: Rory Gallagher was an Irish guitarist and singer known for constant touring, a worn Stratocaster and a direct, powerful take on blues and rock. Many later guitarists name him as a key influence.
know: He first found success with the power trio Taste before going solo in 1971.
His battered 1961 Fender Stratocaster became one of rock's most recognized guitars.
He toured Ireland, including Northern Ireland, steadily through the 1970s, as captured on Irish Tour '74.

influencedBy.why: Gallagher said hearing Lonnie Donegan's skiffle first made him want to play.
Lead Belly's songs were central to his acoustic sets.
Muddy Waters shaped his electric blues and slide playing.
Broonzy's acoustic blues was an early model for his folk-blues side.
His rock and roll drive comes from Chuck Berry.

cousins.why: Hard-touring blues guitarist with a well-worn Stratocaster.
Blues guitar played with rock power.

artists.name: Free
artists.summary: Free was a young British band that stripped blues rock down to space, groove and Paul Rodgers's soul-influenced voice. All Right Now became one of the most played rock songs of the 1970s.
know: The lineup was Paul Rodgers, Paul Kossoff, Andy Fraser and Simon Kirke, all in their teens or barely out of them.
Alexis Korner helped the band get started and gave them their name.
Rodgers and Kirke went on to form Bad Company.

influencedBy.why: Andy Fraser played bass with Mayall before co-founding Free.
Korner championed the young band and gave them their name.
Free's version of The Hunter came from Albert King's Stax recording.
Paul Rodgers modeled his phrasing on Otis Redding and other soul singers.
Paul Kossoff's vibrato-heavy lead style took its starting point from Clapton.

cousins.why: Lean, groove-first songs with lots of space.
Stripped-down, riff-based blues rock.

artists.name: Jeff Beck
artists.summary: Jeff Beck was an English guitarist who kept reinventing rock guitar, from Yardbirds feedback to heavy blues rock to instrumental jazz fusion. Other players have long regarded his touch and tone as unmatched.
know: He replaced Eric Clapton in the Yardbirds in 1965.
The Jeff Beck Group featured Rod Stewart on vocals and Ronnie Wood on bass.
Blow by Blow, produced by George Martin, became a hit instrumental album, and he won eight Grammys over his career.

influencedBy.why: Produced the jazz-rock albums Blow by Blow and Wired.
Produced Hi Ho Silver Lining and Truth.
Beck made a full tribute show and album to Les Paul's music.
His time in the Yardbirds pushed him into feedback and effects.
Buddy Guy's wild, bending blues guitar shaped Beck's early style.
Stevie Wonder wrote Cause We've Ended as Lovers for him and they worked together around Superstition.
Beck recorded People Get Ready with Rod Stewart in 1985.

cousins.why: A guitarist with an instantly recognizable touch.
A guitarist who rewrote what the instrument could do.

artists.name: Paul Butterfield Blues Band
artists.summary: The Paul Butterfield Blues Band was one of the first white American bands to play Chicago electric blues at full strength, with an integrated lineup. They backed Bob Dylan's first electric set and opened rock to long modal jams with East-West.
know: Drummer Sam Lay and bassist Jerome Arnold came from Howlin' Wolf's band.
The band backed Bob Dylan when he went electric at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival.
The title track of East-West mixed blues with Indian raga ideas in a long improvisation.

influencedBy.why: Butterfield learned in Chicago's South Side clubs where Muddy Waters played.
Butterfield's amplified harmonica style follows Little Walter.
The band's rhythm section came from Howlin' Wolf's group.
East-West took its long modal approach from Indian classical music.
Butterfield played with Spann on the 1969 Fathers and Sons sessions and learned from Muddy's band.

cousins.why: A rock-era band devoted to Chicago blues.
Work Song itself, from the soul-jazz side.

artists.name: Canned Heat
artists.summary: Canned Heat was formed by blues record collectors who brought deep pre-war blues knowledge into hippie-era rock. Their hits On the Road Again and Going Up the Country became anthems of the late 1960s.
know: Founders Alan Wilson and Bob Hite were serious collectors of old blues 78s.
Going Up the Country adapts Henry Thomas's 1920s Bull Doze Blues.
They recorded the double album Hooker 'n Heat with John Lee Hooker.

influencedBy.why: Hooker's boogie is the root of their sound, and they recorded a full album with him.
Canned Heat named themselves after his song and recorded his "Big Road Blues."
Alan Wilson worked with Son House in 1964 to help him relearn his songs.
Wilson's high voice owes a debt to Skip James.
Their deep Delta blues knowledge traces back to Patton's records.
Canned Heat covered "Help Me" on their debut.

cousins.why: Hypnotic, driving boogie blues.
Blues-collector rock with a raw edge.

artists.name: Johnny Winter
artists.summary: Johnny Winter was a Texas guitarist known for fast, fierce slide and lead playing in blues and rock. He also produced Muddy Waters's late-career comeback albums.
know: He signed with Columbia in 1969 for one of the largest advances of the time.
His brother is multi-instrumentalist Edgar Winter.
He produced and played on Muddy Waters's Hard Again, I'm Ready and King Bee.

influencedBy.why: Winter called Muddy Waters his hero and later worked closely with him.
B.B. King's lead style was an early model for Winter.
Winter's slide playing draws on Robert Johnson's recordings.
Winter's rock and roll side comes from Chuck Berry, whose songs he often covered.
Texas electric blues starting with T-Bone Walker shaped his playing.

cousins.why: Explosive, high-energy blues guitar.
Texas blues played loud for rock crowds.

artists.name: 13th Floor Elevators
artists.summary: The 13th Floor Elevators were a Texas band that helped invent psychedelic rock, led by Roky Erickson's howling voice and Tommy Hall's electric jug. Their debut was among the first albums to call itself psychedelic.
know: Tommy Hall played an amplified jug, producing a bubbling, warbling sound unique to the band.
Their debut album was among the first to use the word psychedelic in its title.
You're Gonna Miss Me was a regional hit in 1966.
keyAlbums: The Psychedelic Sounds of the 13th Floor Elevators

influencedBy.why: Roky Erickson's screaming vocal style came from Little Richard.
Texas rock and roll from Buddy Holly shaped Erickson's melodies.
Their garage-rock attack follows the British R&B bands.

cousins.why: Wild, inventive 1960s psychedelia from outside the mainstream.
Homemade sound devices at the center of the band.

artists.name: Love
artists.summary: Love was an integrated Los Angeles band led by Arthur Lee, whose third album Forever Changes paired folk rock with orchestral arrangements. It is often ranked among the best albums of the 1960s.
know: Arthur Lee and Bryan MacLean were the band's two songwriters.
They were one of the first rock bands signed to Elektra Records.
Forever Changes used strings and horns arranged by David Angel.
songs: A House Is Not a Motel

influencedBy.why: Love's hit version of My Little Red Book brought his song into garage rock.
Love's early folk rock came straight out of the Byrds' jangling sound.
Their garage-rock edge on 7 and 7 Is draws on the Stones.

cousins.why: Orchestral, psychedelic songwriting from the same era.
Ambitious, orchestrated 1960s pop.

artists.name: Buffalo Springfield
artists.summary: Buffalo Springfield was a short-lived Los Angeles band that brought together Stephen Stills, Neil Young and Richie Furay. In two years it laid the groundwork for country rock and for several major later careers.
know: The band took its name from a steamroller manufacturer.
For What It's Worth, written by Stephen Stills, was their only major hit.
Richie Furay and Jim Messina went on to found Poco, a key country rock band.

influencedBy.why: Signed Buffalo Springfield to Atco.
The Byrds' electric folk rock was the immediate model for the band.
Dylan's writing shaped Stills's and Young's songwriting.
Their studio ambition on Again follows the Beatles' mid-1960s records.
Country songwriting fed Furay's and Young's twangier songs.

cousins.why: Country songcraft in a rock band setting.
Southern California roots-folk with a rock edge.

artists.name: Quicksilver Messenger Service
artists.summary: Quicksilver Messenger Service was a San Francisco band known for twin-guitar improvisation by John Cipollina and Gary Duncan. Their live album Happy Trails captures the extended jamming of the Fillmore era.
know: John Cipollina's trembling, vibrato-heavy guitar tone was the band's signature.
Happy Trails is built around a side-long reworking of Bo Diddley's Who Do You Love.
Pianist Nicky Hopkins played on Shady Grove.

influencedBy.why: Happy Trails is built on long versions of Bo Diddley's Who Do You Love and Mona.
Gold and Silver is based on Brubeck's Take Five.
The band's guitar dueling draws on the Yardbirds' rave-ups.

cousins.why: Long, open improvisation as the main event.
Extended live jams built on a hypnotic groove.

artists.name: Iron Butterfly
artists.summary: Iron Butterfly was a heavy psychedelic band best known for In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida, a 17-minute organ and guitar epic. It was one of the best-selling albums of its era and a step toward heavy metal.
know: The title track of In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida fills an entire side of the album.
It includes a long drum solo by Ron Bushy.
Doug Ingle's dark Hammond organ led the band's sound.

influencedBy.why: Vanilla Fudge's slow, heavy, organ-driven sound was a direct model.
Organ-led dark psychedelia on the West Coast followed the Doors.
Heavy riff rock and long solos came from Cream's example.

cousins.why: Long, heavy grooves that stretch out.
Slow, heavy riffs repeated to hypnotic length.

artists.name: Vanilla Fudge
artists.summary: Vanilla Fudge slowed pop and soul hits down into heavy, dramatic organ-and-drums arrangements. Their approach was a bridge from psychedelia to hard rock and early heavy metal.
know: Their slowed version of the Supremes' You Keep Me Hangin' On was their biggest hit.
Tim Bogert and Carmine Appice later formed Cactus and Beck, Bogert & Appice.
Led Zeppelin opened for them on part of Zeppelin's first US tour.

influencedBy.why: Their breakthrough was a heavy reworking of the Supremes' hit.
Their debut includes slowed, dramatic versions of several Beatles songs.
Mark Stein's organ-led blue-eyed soul sound followed the Rascals.

cousins.why: Slowed, extended reworkings of pop hits.
Hammond organ grooves at the center.

artists.name: Syd Barrett
artists.summary: Syd Barrett was the founding singer, guitarist and main songwriter of Pink Floyd, whose whimsical, strange songs defined early English psychedelia. After leaving the band he made two fragile solo albums.
know: He wrote most of Pink Floyd's debut, The Piper at the Gates of Dawn.
He left Pink Floyd in 1968 and was replaced by David Gilmour.
Roger Waters and David Gilmour helped produce his solo albums.
keyAlbums: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn (Pink Floyd)

influencedBy.why: Pink Floyd's Interstellar Overdrive grew from a riff based on Love's My Little Red Book.
Barrett's English, whimsical pop draws on mid-1960s Beatles.
Early Pink Floyd sets were built on R&B like Bo Diddley.

cousins.why: Fragile, haunting English songs.
Playful, strange 1960s psychedelia.

artists.name: The Pretty Things
artists.summary: The Pretty Things were one of the rawest British R&B bands of the 1960s and later made S.F. Sorrow, an early rock opera. They are often named as a link between beat music, psychedelia and punk.
know: Guitarist Dick Taylor had played in an early version of the Rolling Stones.
S.F. Sorrow, recorded at Abbey Road, is one of the first rock concept albums built on a story.
David Bowie covered Rosalyn and Don't Bring Me Down on Pin Ups.

influencedBy.why: The band took its name from Bo Diddley's song Pretty Thing.
Dick Taylor came from the Stones' first lineup.
Their early R&B sets leaned on Jimmy Reed songs.
Their raw early sound came from Chuck Berry rock and roll.

cousins.why: Wild, loud R&B-based rock.
Raw, aggressive garage rock.

artists.name: Traffic
artists.summary: Traffic was Steve Winwood's band, mixing English folk, jazz, soul and psychedelia into long, loose arrangements. Their open, improvising style shaped later roots and jam rock.
know: Steve Winwood came from the Spencer Davis Group and joined Blind Faith in 1969.
The band wrote its early songs in a cottage in rural Berkshire.
Dave Mason's Feelin' Alright? became a hit for Joe Cocker.
keyAlbums: The Low Spark of High Heeled Boys
songs: The Low Spark of High Heeled Boys

influencedBy.why: David Hood and Roger Hawkins toured and recorded with Traffic in 1973.
Winwood's soulful singing and organ come straight from Ray Charles.
Chris Wood's jazz flute and sax and the band's long jams draw on modal jazz.
Their early psychedelic singles come out of the Beatles' 1967 sound.

cousins.why: Jazz-based group improvisation.
Soulful keyboard-led singing.

artists.name: Small Faces
artists.summary: Small Faces were the leading mod band of 1960s London, pairing Steve Marriott's soul voice with tight R&B and later psychedelic pop. Their influence runs through British rock from the Jam to Britpop.
know: The lineup was Steve Marriott, Ronnie Lane, Kenney Jones and Ian McLagan.
Ogdens' Nut Gone Flake came in a round sleeve shaped like a tobacco tin and reached number one in the UK.
After Marriott left, the others joined Rod Stewart and Ron Wood to form Faces.

influencedBy.why: Ian McLagan's Hammond style came from Booker T. & the M.G.'s.
Marriott modeled his singing on Stax soul.
Marriott's gritty R&B vocals follow Ray Charles.
Their tight soul grooves draw on James Brown.

cousins.why: High-energy soul singing.
Gritty, shouted R&B vocals.

artists.name: Faces
artists.summary: Faces were a loose, rowdy British rock band formed from Small Faces with Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood. Their ragged, warm sound became a template for bar-band rock and roll.
know: The band formed when Small Faces' remaining members joined Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood from the Jeff Beck Group.
Rod Stewart ran a solo career alongside the band, often with the same players.
Ronnie Wood joined the Rolling Stones in 1975.
keyAlbums: A Nod Is as Good as a Wink... to a Blind Horse
songs: Had Me a Real Good Time

influencedBy.why: Stewart and Ronnie Wood went from the Beck Group to Faces.
Lane, Jones and McLagan formed Faces after Small Faces split.
Rod Stewart has named Sam Cooke as his main vocal model.
Their loose, blues-based rock and roll runs parallel to the Stones.
Their bar-band drive comes from Chuck Berry rock and roll.

cousins.why: Ragged, warm bar-band rock with a storyteller's heart.
Rowdy, good-time band energy with real songs.

artists.name: The Hollies
artists.summary: The Hollies are a Manchester band famous for bright three-part harmonies and a long run of hit singles. Graham Nash left them to form Crosby, Stills & Nash.
know: Allan Clarke and Graham Nash were childhood friends who started the band.
Graham Nash left in 1968 and co-founded Crosby, Stills & Nash.
Elton John, then a session player, played piano on He Ain't Heavy, He's My Brother.
songs: He Ain't Heavy, He's My Brother
Long Cool Woman in a Black Dress

influencedBy.why: Engineered The Air That I Breathe, one of the Hollies' biggest late hits.
The Hollies' close harmony singing comes from the Everly Brothers.
The band's name was partly a nod to Buddy Holly.
They rose in the British beat boom the Beatles led.
The Hollies had an early hit with a cover of Searchin'.

cousins.why: Bright, stacked vocal harmonies on pop singles.
Close two-voice harmony at the heart of the songs.

artists.name: The Troggs

Their simple rock and roll base comes from Chuck Berry.
They came up in the British R&B beat scene.

Primitive, blunt riffs and simple beats.

artists.name: The Sonics

Raw, screaming proto-punk.

artists.name: Steppenwolf

artists.name: Blue Cheer

Their cover of Eddie Cochran's Summertime Blues reached the US Top 20 in 1968.

artists.name: The Young Rascals

artists.name: Chicago

artists.name: John Lennon
